In FDG-avid lymphomas (Hodgkin and most aggressive non-Hodgkin lymphomas) PET-CT is the reference staging examination: it finds involved nodes even when not enlarged, the spleen and the bone marrow, and often makes bone marrow biopsy unnecessary.
The stage is assigned with the Lugano classification: what matters is on which side of the diaphragm the involved stations are and whether there is disease outside the nodes. Bulky disease must also be reported, because it changes treatment.
Pitfalls: brown fat (neck, supraclavicular and paravertebral regions; more frequent in young people and in the cold), thymus in young patients after chemotherapy, muscle, bowel and urinary uptake. The fused CT shows whether the uptake falls in a lymph node.
The staging PET is also the baseline for response: follow-up PETs are read with the Deauville score.
